metadata.title: Stale, Not Broken.
metadata.subtitle: The Debug-Plugins Skill (Claude Tag Plugin)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when a plugin or the skill inside it doesn't show up, is the configuration broken — or is something else going on? Lands the carry-out that a missing plugin needs evidence (what arrived, what loaded) before a diagnosis, and that a setting change needs a fresh chat, not a refresh.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed a plugin that won't show up means broken configuration. Usually it's just stale, read once, when the session started. So — is my config broken, or just out of date?

beats.narration_text: Before deciding anything, Claude checks three things in order: what actually arrived in the plugin mount, what flags Claude Code was launched with, and what the startup log recorded. All three get collected before any explanation is offered.

Then it walks a short list of causes. The zip simply isn't there. It's there, but Claude Code wasn't launched with a matching flag. The zip failed to extract. The plugin's manifest file is malformed — often just a stray capital letter or space in the name. Or the zip is fine, but the skill file's own header is broken.

Two limits worth knowing. First: a session reads your configuration once, when it starts — flip a setting mid-chat, and the fix is a new conversation, not a refresh of this one. Second: some of Claude Code's startup errors go to a channel this diagnostic can't see — so a clean-looking log doesn't guarantee nothing went wrong, it just means this particular channel didn't catch it.
If a plugin won't show up, check what actually arrived and what actually loaded before assuming it's broken — and if you just flipped a setting, open a new chat before you diagnose anything else.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code: A plugin zip is sitting in slash mnt slash account-plugins, but the skill inside it isn't showing up. Walk me through what actually arrived, what you were launched with, and what the startup log says, before telling me what's wrong. Then check three things. Does it collect all three before explaining anything? Does it say so if the log file is missing, instead of skipping past it? And if you flipped the setting a few minutes ago, does it ask you to start a fresh conversation?

output: Watch for: all three steps before any explanation
